"executive_summary": "This paper establishes a Lusin-type characterisation of Hardy spaces associated with the Hermite operator L = −Δ + |x|² on R^d, for d ≥ 3 and index p ∈ (0, 1]. The central object is the space H^p_L(R^d), defined as the completion of {f ∈ L²(R^d) : M_L f ∈ L^p(R^d)} under the quasi-norm ‖·‖_{H^p_L} = ‖M_L ·‖_{L^p}, where M_L f(·) = sup_{t>0} |e^{−tL} f(·)|. The authors introduce a Lusin integral S f(x) built from the Poisson semigroup P_t associated with L and from Hermite-specific first-order derivatives ∂_j + x_j, and define the space H^p_S(R^d) accordingly. The main theorem (Theorem 1.1) proves that (H^p_L(R^d), ‖·‖_{H^p_L}) equals (H^p_S(R^d), ‖·‖_{H^p_S}) as quasi-normed spaces. The proof proceeds through two intermediate spaces: H^p_{L,max}(R^d), defined via a maximal Poisson function f*_L, and H^p_A(R^d), defined via an area-integral operator A. The inclusion H^p_L ⊂ H^p_{L,max} is shown in Section 3, and the equality H^p_L = H^p_A ∩ L² is established in Section 4 using atom decompositions and tent spaces. Section 5 proves the main theorem, combining these results with an approximation argument. Section 6 proves Theorem 1.2, that the Riesz transforms R^L_j = (∂_j + x_j) L^{−1/2} are bounded on H^p_L(R^d). The work extends prior results that were restricted to p = 1 (cf. [Jiz12]) and to p = 1 on spaces of homogeneous type (cf. [HLM+11, Chapter 4]). The approach is distinguished by using the more general Lusin area integrals defined with derivatives ∂_j + x_j, which were first suggested by Thangavelu in [Tha90] and are specific to Hermite operators. The paper is entirely theoretical, with no numerical experiments, datasets, or computational benchmarks; all results are analytic identities and boundedness statements. The technical apparatus includes kernel estimates for the semigroups generated by L and L^{1/2}, atom decompositions, generalized Hölder inequalities, Calderón reproducing formulas, and interpolation. The results hold for the range d/(d+δ) < p ≤ 1, where δ is a Hölder-type exponent arising from the kernel smoothness estimates.",
